 Tested and vetted at IGN.
 By  Eric Song Updated : Nov 10, 2026 10:17pm UTC Add IGN on Google 0 1 Looking for a good price (nowadays) for a reliable Switch 2 memory card? Ahead of Black Friday, Amazon has dropped the price of the highly rated Samsung P9 512GB Micro SDXC Express Card from $150 to $99.99 with free shipping. Alternatively, the 256GB model has also dropped in price from $80 to $47.99. Are these the lowest prices ever? No. Are there cheaper memory cards out there? Yes . But if you're looking for a memory card that we've personally tested and recommend , you won't find a better deal today.
 Samsung P9 Nintendo Switch Memory Cards on Sale
 Samsung P9 512GB MicroSD Express Card
 29 Nintendo Switch 2 compatible $149.99 save 33% $99.99 at Amazon Samsung P9 256GB MicroSD Express Card
 14 Nintendo Switch 2 Compatible $54.99 save 13% $47.99 at Amazon The Switch 2 only comes with 256GB of onboard storage and it will run out faster than you think. If you have a standard MicroSD card from your previous Switch, it won't work on the Switch 2. Although the two might look similar, the MicroSD Express card is much faster than its predecessor. The Samsung P9 model boasts transfer speeds of up to 800MB/s.
 Quite a few games have now been released for the Switch 2 and some of them require an enormous amount of space. Final Fantasy 14 is the most gigabyte-hungry game to date, requiring about 117GB all by itself. That game alone takes up half of the Switch 2's internal storage capacity. Other plus-sized games include Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade (90GB), Split Fiction (70GB), Cyberpunk 2077 (60GB), and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment (44GB). The upcoming The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will top out at about 27GB. Nowadays it's completely possible to download just three or four games and find yourself completely out of onboard storage.
